title: Do not treat inferred non-search search-term rows as literal shopper queries
scenario: A Sponsored Products Search Term report contains a clicked row whose displayed search term came from a non-search context where Amazon inferred a best match. The row is inefficient and the analyst is asked to harvest or negate the displayed string as if it were a shopper-entered query.

inputs.requested_output: This search term wastes money. Add it as Negative Exact and also create an Exact keyword only if you think the term has future value.

forbidden_behaviors: Describe the displayed search term as a confirmed shopper-entered query despite the supplied inferred non-search origin.
Recommend action-safe Negative Exact solely from the displayed string and poor performance.
Recommend Exact keyword harvesting solely because the report row contains a search-term string.
Treat the inferred best-match text as proof of shopper intent.
required_observations: The row is a valid observed traffic/performance signal, but its displayed string is an inferred best match from non-search traffic rather than confirmed literal shopper-query text.
Negative keyword or Exact-harvest decisions require evidence that the displayed term maps to the intended keyword control and literal query semantics.
The next diagnostic step should inspect matched targeting, placement/traffic context, and any literal-query evidence before choosing the control to change.

rubric.requirement: Distinguish literal shopper-query text from inferred non-search best-match text.
Do not map a report string directly to Negative Exact or Exact harvest when the observed traffic came from a different or uncertain control path.
Use spend/conversion evidence for traffic-quality diagnosis without overstating what it proves about shopper intent.
Keep the decision directional/hold/manual-review until term origin and control mapping support a safe action.
